utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone in this courtroom, and good morning also to those assisting us just outside the courtroom. Madam Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honour. This is case number IT-96-23/2-PT, the Prosecutor versus Dragan Zelenovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. May I have the appearances. Prosecution first, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honour. My name is Hildegard Uertz-Retzlaff, and I appear today together with Trial Attorney Mr. Manoj Sachdeva and our case manager Verica Balikic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Uertz-Retzlaff. And for the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honour. My name is Zoran Jovanovic. I am an attorney from Belgrade, and I am representing the accused, Dragan Zelenovic. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Jovanovic. Mr. Zelenovic, first question is whether you can hear me and can hear the other participants in this -- in this Status Conference in a language you understand.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You may remain seated, Mr. Zelenovic. Mr. Zelenovic, this is a Status Conference, the first Status Conference in your case, and it's unrelated to another hearing we recently had, which is the hearing under Rule 11 bis. At that hearing the possibility of your case to be referred to the former Yugoslavia was the subject of discussion, whereas at this Status Conference we are focusing on where the parties stand as far as trial preparation here in The Hague is concerned. This Status Conference was supposed to take place within 120 days from the initial appearance, but due to unavailability of counsel it was rescheduled and now takes place at a little bit of this time-limit. I'd like to address the parties. Are there any disclosure issues outstanding at this moment? Perhaps I should address you, Mr. Jovanovic, because you're the one who should receive any disclosed material. Are there any issues outstanding in that respect?

utterances.speaker: MR. JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. Not for the time being. The Defence is in constant contact with the Prosecution, and we have received materials from the Kunjarac and others case which is relevant for the present case, the written statements by the accused, transcripts of the public hearings, and the transcripts have been translated so that the accused can also read those materials. And before I arrived here, we received materials pursuant to Rule 68 from the Prosecution. I have not yet been able to inspect it, but we have had no problems in this regard whatsoever.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Madam Uertz-Retzlaff, are there any surprises to be expected or -- while you know that sometimes disclosure issues suddenly come up. Is there any reason to assume that such surprises would be there in the near future?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: No, Your Honour, we have actually completed the disclosure of both Rule 66 material and Rule 68 material and there are no surprises to be expected.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's good to hear. Then the next item I'd like to ask you about is the following. We come to a point where soon I think the Prosecution would meet, perhaps, with the Defence and with the Senior Legal Officer and to see when pre-trial briefs could be submitted, witness lists, et cetera. Although the case is not expected to be tried very soon, but let's say within the next three months, would the Prosecution be in a position to -- to tell the Court when pre-trial briefs could be submitted and when witness lists, exhibit lists, et cetera, could be produced?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, since the initial appearance we are in constant discussion with the Defence, and I think we can finalise all pre-trial issues within this week, I hope. We have a meeting with the Defence today, and I hope the result will actually enable us to wrap up the case within a week or two, perhaps, and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So then the Chamber will hear soon from -- well, any scheduling issues --

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- as far as pre-trial preparations are concerned?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you for that. Mr. Jovanovic, I see that you seem to agree with Madam Uertz-Retzlaff on pre-trial issues to be resolved relatively soon.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, that's what I expect, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then as a matter of fact as far as trial preparations and further developments are concerned, there seems to be nothing more to be discussed, unless you, Madam Uertz-Retzlaff, or you, Mr. Jovanovic, would have any issue to be raised at this moment. I'll come later to the more personal issues like health and detention situation.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Nothing from the Prosecution, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Nothing from the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, we have no issues that the Defence would like to raise, and as you say you will be asking questions about the health and some personal circumstances of the accused, but this is something that either the Defence or the accused may answer depending on your instructions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then I also think - but please correct me when I'm wrong - that there are no pending motions at this moment. I think the last decision by this Trial Chamber was delivered on the 11th of October, which decided the preliminary motion filed by the Defence on the form of the indictment, which was -- the motion was denied, but I don't think that there are any other motions pending, that there are any issues apart from disclosure and pre-trial developments.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I agree, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then finally, I'd like to address you personally, Mr. Zelenovic. Are there any health issues or any detention issues you would like to raise, either by yourself or through counsel? And I inform you that if any of the -- if there's any health issue to be raised, that you always can ask to go into private session because health issues are not necessarily to be heard in public. Yes, I hear from Mr. Jovanovic. Mr. Jovanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, thank you. I don't think there is any need for us to go into private session. We will not be going into any details. The health of the accused, Dragan Zelenovic, has deteriorated substantially, and I -- I received the medical documents from the UN Detention Unit, and now let me just give you a very brief summary of the report with a diagnosis and his general health condition, this is here in this report, and the Defence has contacted both the Registry and the relevant bodies in the UN Detention Unit. So this is being dealt with.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. So I do understand that although the health situation has been deteriorated that proper medical care is provided. Is that how I can understand your words?

utterances.speaker: MR. JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. The accused has underwent -- has undergone medical examinations in hospitals, so not only in the UN Detention Unit. He's being treated in the UN Detention Unit, and the accused has no objections to the therapy he's receiving right now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you for that information. That as far as the medical condition of you, Mr. Zelenovic, is concerned. Is there any detention issue which you would like to bring to my attention?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Zelenovic, if you would sit down, then we would be better able to follow you because you're so far away from the microphone. Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I have no problems in the Detention Unit, but I have problems when I'm transported to the Tribunal. I have nothing to wear. I have spent the last -- the last year in detention, and when I come here for a hearing I have to borrow clothes. Because when I was in detention in Russia I was told that I should buy some clothes in -- when I was in jail there, and I even painted some rooms for them, but nothing happened in the end.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Well, that's an issue that does not immediately affect the proceedings before this Trial Chamber, but I do understand -- I fully understand that you feel not very comfortable if you don't have your own clothes, which is in many systems specifically a right for those who are not yet tried to have their own clothes available. Did you try to get in touch with your family to have any clothing sent or -- I must admit that I'm not fully familiar with how you would buy clothes in a detention situation. I take it that there must be some possibility. At least it's good that you have drawn the attention to this issue, which seems to be an issue primarily within the responsibility of the Registry because it concerns the detention situation. Have you been in touch with your family to see whether you could resolve it?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I wrote to the government of the Republika Srpska through the Registry, and the response that I got was, We cannot help them in any way. They cannot get a ticket to -- for my family to come here. I have been here for six months without any contact with my family. My family has been unable to visit us, and the Republika Srpska government says, Well, we didn't surrender him. He was transferred here from Russia by the Russian authorities to the Federation, so this has nothing to do with us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I do understand the situation. Again, it's good that you've drawn our attention to it because I can understand how uncomfortable it is for you, and it seems to be a problem which perhaps, also with the help of your counsel, seems not an insurmountable problem. Mr. Jovanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. Mr. Zelenovic's wife, who lives in Foca, is a very poor financial status, and that has been established in the course of the proceedings to establish his financial status in order to assign counsel. On several occasions, I contacted Mr. Zelenovic's sister in Belgrade. She sent some money to him and some warm clothing that he can use during walks in the Detention Unit, but that is all. I'm always here to -- available to bring him whatever his family sends. I also addressed the office for the cooperation with the ICTY and the government of Republika Srpska, but they told me that the decision concerning assistance that was in application before is now not in force any longer and that they have absolutely no means to help Mr. Zelenovic any longer. I am at your disposal for any contact that I can make, and every time I come to visit I will bring whatever his family sends him. He is in telephone contact with his family, and I suppose it is up to his family whether they are going to send him money, clothes, or whatever else.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Jovanovic, I have been Defence counsel in the past and I could not imagine that any of my clients in the past finally would not have some clothes of their own in which they could appear in court. It is -- I see it that as a problem who would pay for it, but finally I could not imagine that I would not with some inventivity resolve that problem, and I take it that you have difficulties to imagine yourself that not in any way you could resolve this problem.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, yes, I feel the same way as you, and I look at things the same way as you do. And if I'm allowed to be creative, the problem will be resolved. I will do everything in my power to resolve the problem within the framework of the Rules of Procedure of this Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. It is good to hear that you also consider the problem one that could and should be resolved. Any other detention issue, Mr. Zelenovic?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is there any other matter to be raised at this moment?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Jovanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then we'll adjourn sine die.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: adjourned at 10.23 a.m.
